one_sentence_story: In his 1968 Science landmark, Columbia psychologist Stanley Schachter secretly ran laboratory wall dials at half-speed (5:20 PM) or double-speed (6:05 PM) while real time was 5:35 PM — proving external visual cues ('It's dinner time!', bright lights on cashews, food left on the desk) can double snacking right past internal stomach fullness.
so_what_for_you: Redesign your kitchen sightlines instead of fighting exhausting willpower battles: keep nutritious food in bright eye-level bowls, store treats inside **opaque closed cabinets**, and check true physical stomach hunger before eating just because the screen says 12:00.
